papers.what_it_is: A preprint arguing, with a classical surrogate built from Pauli propagation, tensor networks and classical shadows, that tracing out and measurement-based QCNNs are effectively classically simulable on the locally-easy benchmark datasets used in the literature.

papers.title_in_file: NoRA: A Tensor Network Ansatz for Volume-Law Entangled Equilibrium States of Highly Connected Hamiltonians
papers.version_note: arXiv:2303.16946v5, 20 May 2024; the Quantum published version (accepted 2024-04-08). The text layer matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: A theory and numerics paper that proposes a non-local layered tensor network (NoRA) for volume-law ground spaces of all-to-all models such as SYK, and studies it as a random-Clifford stabilizer code.

existing.note: The abstract claim is stated without a proof. The numerical support is approximate: the Section 4.2.1 and Figure 11 text says the trend 'might coincide' with the quantum singleton bound limit and that more data is needed to prove it, and the distances come from Monte Carlo sampling that gives only an upper bound. The Section 4.3 summary is stronger ('we verified'). Linear distance is also tied to the layer depth being large enough in Section 5.1 and 5.3.
existing.value: The authors state that the SYK-inspired code family can be chosen to have constant rate and linear distance at the cost of some high weight stabilizers. They describe the numerical trend toward a constant relative distance as only approximate and state that more data is needed to prove it.
existing.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Figure 11 caption, p.13; Section 4.2.1, p.13
quotes: We introduce a family of codes inspired by the SYK model which can be chosen to have constant rate and linear distance at the cost of some high weight stabilizers.
we can see that both trends might coincide in that very limit, or at least come close.
However more data is needed to be able to prove this.
existing.certainty_reason: The authors' own claim, supported by approximate numerics; the paper says more data is needed to prove it.
existing.reader_inference: The distance is estimated by random sampling of regions, which the paper says gives only an upper bound, so the numerical support does not by itself establish a linear lower bound.

quotes: We argue that the architecture is potentially expressive enough to capture the entanglement and complexity of the ground space of the SYK model, thus making it a suitable variational ansatz, but we leave a detailed study of SYK to future work.
existing.certainty_reason: The authors' own claim, not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors define the NoRA network as layers of quantum circuits in which each layer acts on the qudits output by the previous layer together with additional new ancillary thermal qudits initialized in the |0⟩ state, and state that the layer circuits do not have to respect locality.
quotes: For each layer 1 ≤ ℓ ≤ L the circuit Dℓ acts on the nℓ−1 qudit output from the previous layer and an additional ∆nℓ new ancillary “thermal” qudits initialized in state |0⟩.
We stress that the layer circuits Dℓ do not have to respect locality structure depicted by the 1d arrangement of qudit lines.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its own architecture in the Figure 1 caption.

assertions.value: The authors state that the networks they consider can be viewed as generalizations of MERA, DMERA and branching MERA networks in which the requirement of spatial locality is removed.
quotes: The networks we consider can be viewed as generalizations of MERA, DMERA, and branching MERA networks where the requirement of spatial locality is removed
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state how they define the architecture relative to MERA variants.

assertions.value: The authors state that they primarily consider a scaling case in which the number of thermal qudits increases exponentially with each layer up from the bottom, and that they primarily consider the growth rate r = 2.
quotes: we will primarily consider the special case where nℓ ∼ k + rℓ, so that the number of thermal qudits is increasing exponentially with each layer up from the bottom.
For the case of r = 2, which we primarily consider

assertions.value: The authors state that the circuit has a number of non-trivial bonds that grows linearly with the system size, with as many bonds as there are qudits connecting to the same constant-depth circuit in the last layer, and that it is therefore straightforward to establish that the network has the potential to encode volume law entanglement for sub-regions of a typical UV state.
quotes: There are O(N ) nontrivial bonds in the circuit, of which N bonds connect to the same constant-depth circuit in the last layer.
It is therefore straightforward to establish that the network has the potential to encode volume law entanglement for sub-regions of a “typical” UV state.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors assert this from a bond-counting argument; the explicit demonstration is the Clifford numerics.

assertions.certainty_reason: The authors define their complexity measure and state its limit in Section 2.3.

assertions.value: The authors introduce a toy Hamiltonian for which the network is an exact ground state for any choice of state on the k ground state qudits, so that the toy Hamiltonian has an exactly degenerate ground space.
quotes: The idea is to introduce a toy Hamiltonian for which the above network is an exact ground state for any choice of state on the k ground state qudits.
In other words, the toy Hamiltonian has an exactly degenerate ground space.

assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of the toy Hamiltonian in Section 2.4.

assertions.value: The authors report, for L = 20, r = 2, k = 1, d = 2, Λ = 1 and γ = 0.4, that the exact Gibbs entropy of the toy Hamiltonian and its low-temperature approximation match almost exactly at small T/Λ, with a fitted log-log slope of 1.7304 ± 0.0004 for the exact entropy, and they take this as confirming a scaling law.

assertions.value: The authors state that, for an appropriate choice of parameters, the toy model can exhibit a power-law temperature dependence of the thermodynamic entropy and therefore the heat capacity, and in the low-temperature limit they derive an upper bound on the continuum entropy that scales with (βΛ)−α/γ = (T /Λ)α/γ (the exponent printed flat in the text layer).

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains to be shown that the weight trend occurs for different choices of g and r and continues for larger a and b, and that they intend to explore the phase transition for large L in future work.
quotes: It remains to be shown that this trend occurs for different choices of g and r and continues as expected for larger a and b.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this open item in Section 4.2.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that through numerical simulations they verified that the stabilizer codes from random Clifford layers can have volumelaw entanglement and a relative distance approaching a non-zero constant as N → ∞, and that the architecture can produce a family of codes with non-vanishing relative distance and rate at the cost of having some high weight stabilizers.
quotes: we verified that the stabilizer codes obtained from the random Clifford layers indeed can have volumelaw entanglement
and relative distance approaching a non-zero constant in the thermodynamic limit N → ∞.
Our architecture with random layers is therefor capable of producing a family of codes indexed by N with non-vanishing relative distance and rate at the cost of having some high weight stabilizers
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' summary of their numerical results.
assertions.reader_inference: The summary says 'verified', while Section 4.2.1 and the Figure 11 caption say more data is needed to prove the convergence; the paper also gives no direct comparison with a fully random code, although the summary says the high weight stabilizers are significantly fewer than in such a code.

assertions.value: The authors state that they find the network can produce good quantum codes, meaning code families where the distance and the number of logical qudits are both proportional to the number of physical qudits, but that these codes are not LDPC codes since some of the stabilizers are high weight.
quotes: We find that the network can produce good quantum codes [42], meaning code families where the distance and number of logical qudits are both proportional to the number of physical qudits.
However, these codes are not low-density parity check (LDPC) codes [43, 44] since some of the stabilizers are high weight.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own claim, based on the approximate numerics of Section 4.

assertions.value: The authors hypothesize that by further fine-tuning the gates, the architecture could also yield encoding circuits for the recently discovered classes of good quantum LDPC codes, and state that producing a good quantum LDPC code is the challenge of keeping the weights of checks low while keeping the distance high, which clearly requires tuning of the layer circuits.
quotes: We hypothesize that by further fine-tuning the gates, our network architecture could also yield encoding circuits for the recently discovered classes of good quantum LDPC codes [45–50].
This clearly requires tuning of the layer circuits, likely made possible by the addition of some structure to the problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: A hypothesis of the authors, not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the SYK-inspired code the number of gates has a leading N log N scaling with the total number of degrees of freedom, which they compare with holographic complexity conjectures for JT gravity, and state that they have an explicit estimate and upper bound of order N ln N for the circuit complexity of the ground space of the code Hamiltonian.
quotes: This leading N log N scaling with the total number of degrees of freedom can be compared to holographic complexity conjectures applied to JT gravity [59]
We have an explicit estimate (and upper bound) of O(N ln N ) for circuit complexity of the ground space of Hcode.
assertions.certainty_reason: A gate-count estimate that the authors say is in general only an upper bound on circuit complexity.

assertions.value: The authors caution that the random Clifford layer model is certainly not correct for the actual SYK model, because the gates must act on fermionic degrees of freedom and will generically not be Clifford.
quotes: We caution that this is certainly not correct for the actual SYK model: the gates must act on fermionic degrees of freedom and will not be Clifford (or the fermionic analogue of Clifford) generically.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of the Clifford model in Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors assume that a typical logical operator grows in size by a factor of gD after passing through one layer, up to a maximum size set by the total number of qudits, and compare this growth with the ratio of qudit numbers in successive layers to estimate the distance of the SYK-inspired code.
quotes: Let us assume that a typical operator grows in size by a factor of gD after passing through one layer (i.e. being conjugated by that layer unitary), up to a maximum size set by the total number of qudits.
We must compare this operator growth to the rate of qudit increase.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the assumption of their distance estimate in Section 5.1.

assertions.value: The authors state, as an analytic estimate under the operator growth model, that when gD exceeds r the distance is expected to be linear in N, and that when gD is below r the logical operators are supported on a dilute fraction of sites and the distance is expected to scale as a sublinear function of N.

quotes: In this case, we expect the distance to be
linear in N .
Alternatively, if gD < r, then the distance could be some power of N , N c.
Suppose gD < RL. Then there will be some layer ℓ∗ such that operator growth and qudit growth
assertions.certainty_reason: An analytic estimate that rests on the operator growth assumption; the authors write 'expect' and 'could be'.

assertions.value: The authors state that they expect the stabilizer weights to show a pattern similar to Figure 10, with a non-zero fraction of constant weight stabilizers from the UV-most layer and at least a few stabilizers of very high weight, similar to the weight of logical operators.
quotes: We expect that the stabilizer weights will display a similar pattern as in Figure 10.
In particular, there are at least a few stabilizers of very high weight, similar to the weight of logical operators.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' expectation for the thermodynamic-limit family, not tested separately.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SYK Hamiltonian has a number of weight-4 terms that do not all commute, with random coefficients, whereas the code Hamiltonian has commuting terms with fixed coefficients and many low-weight terms but a significant fraction of high-weight terms; they also state that the code Hamiltonian has an exactly degenerate ground space and a spectrum that is not random-matrix-like, while the SYK Hamiltonian has approximately degenerate ground states and a random-matrix-like spectrum.
quotes: These terms do not all commute and they enter HSYK with random coefficients. Hcode is composed of O(N ) commuting terms with fixed coefficients.
The fine-grained energy spectrum of HSYK is random-matrixlike [61, 62]. The fine-grained energy spectrum of Hcode is not random-matrix-like because Hcode is a commuting projector Hamiltonian.
However, there are also crucial differences between the two.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state these differences between the code Hamiltonian and the SYK model in Section 5.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that both the SYK Hamiltonian and the code Hamiltonian have eigenstates with volume-law entanglement, that eigenstates of the code Hamiltonian have a flat entanglement spectrum, that the parameters of the code Hamiltonian can be chosen so that its low temperature heat capacity is proportional to T, and that the many similarities are the basis for their conjecture that the architecture has the potential to describe SYK physics once the tensors are adapted to a particular SYK instance.
quotes: Entanglement: Both models feature Hamiltonian eigenstates with volume-law entanglement.
In particular, eigenstates of Hcode, being stabilizer states, have a flat entanglement spectrum.
Similarly, the parameters of Hcode can be chosen so that its low temperature heat capacity is proportional to T .
The many similarities between HSYK and Hcode are the basis for our conjecture that the architecture in Figure 1 has the potential to describe the physics of the SYK model
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' comparison and conjecture; the SYK side is not computed in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that the approximate ground space of the SYK model could have interesting properties as an approximate quantum error correction code, that the distance of this code is not immediately clear, and that they defer a full discussion to future work.
quotes: This naturally raises the possibility that the approximate ground space of the SYK model could have interesting properties as an approximate quantum error correction code.
What is not immediately clear is the distance of this code.
We will defer a full discussion to a future work
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own speculation, not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that the analysis of the SYK-inspired model suggests that the SYK ground space code, which has constant rate as N → ∞, could have a distance N to a power c for some constant 0 < c ≤ 1, and that, given the relatively low scaling dimension of the fermion operators, it may be that one is effectively in the gD < r regime.
quotes: the analysis of the SYK-inspired model suggests that the actual SYK ground space code, which has constant rate as N → ∞, could have a distance N c for some constant 0 < c ≤ 1.
Given the relatively low scaling dimension of the fermion operators, it may be that one is effectively in the gD < r regime.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' speculation drawn from a model analysis, not tested on SYK.

assertions.value: The authors describe a construction that takes the encoding circuits for two [[n, k, δ]] codes and mixes their physical qubits with an additional depth D circuit, giving a code on n′ = 2n qubits with k′ = 2k and the same rate, and state that the distance will also increase by a factor with some probability.
quotes: The result is a code on n′ = 2n qubits with k′ = 2k. Hence, the rate is the same, k′/n′ = k/n. The distance will also increase by a factor with some probability, as will the weights of the stabilizers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors describe a construction and an expectation; no numerical test of it is reported.

assertions.value: The authors state that they intend to find alternative bases of the stabilizer code that minimize the overall weights, that the reduced-row echelon form is unique, and that it is intuitively clear that it maximizes the number of zero-valued elements and thus minimizes the weights of the stabilizer basis elements.
quotes: In the exact case, such a basis is unique and given by the reduced-row echelon form (RREF) of the stabilizer matrix
From this it should be intuitively clear that the RREF maximizes the number of zero-valued elements in the matrix, thus minimizing the weights of the stabilizer basis elements.
assertions.certainty_reason: An intuitive argument by the authors, with a plan to test it in future work.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper gives only an example matrix; whether the reduced-row echelon form gives the minimum weight over all bases of the stabilizer group is not shown here and is not obvious.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing perturbative gadgets, that using order-w perturbation theory it can be shown that there exists a 2-local Hamiltonian that approximately has the same ground space, constructed with w · (n − k) ancillary qudits, and that they expect the ground state degeneracy and code properties to be unaffected although the terms might not commute any more.
quotes: Using wth-order perturbation theory it can then be shown that there must exist a 2-local Hamiltonian that approximately has the same ground space i.e. the desired quantum error-correcting code.
its construction involves introducing w · (n − k) ancillary qudits
but we expect the ground state degeneracy and code properties to be unaffected.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work (reference 64), plus an expectation of the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that the first step toward closer contact with SYK is to develop a fermionic analogue of the architecture, that for the q = 2 SYK model, a non-interacting fermion model, they can efficiently simulate the network with non-interacting fermion machinery, and that they are currently exploring this direction.
quotes: The first step is to develop a fermionic analogue of our architecture.
A related setting where we should be able to carry out classical simulations is the SYK model for q = 2, i.e. a non-interacting fermion model with random all-to-all hoppings.
In this case, we can efficiently simulate the network using non-interacting fermion machinery.
We are currently exploring this direction.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' statements of plan and expectation, not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that a single-layer NoRA plausibly captures the ground state of the transverse field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at large and at small transverse field, that it is less clear at the critical point, and that these are plausibility arguments for which a more systematic study is future work.
quotes: Hence, it is plausibly the case that a NoRA with one layer could capture the ground state of the TFSK
Finally, at the critical point separating the two phases, it is less clear whether NoRA is suitable or not
We emphasize that these are plausibility arguments.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own plausibility arguments, which they state are not a systematic study.

assertions.value: The authors state that their architecture mimics the structure of two-dimensional Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity in AdS2, interpreting the logarithm of the radial coordinate as analogous to L − ℓ, and that the NoRA network can be viewed as a refinement of a matrix product state model in which the tensors have additional layer structure.
quotes: The basic point is that our architecture mimics the structure of two-dimensional Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity in AdS2.
we can view the NoRA network model as a refinement of the matrix product state model
assertions.certainty_reason: An analogy asserted by the authors; no computation in the paper tests it.

assertions.value: The authors state that for a state with a flat entanglement spectrum, meaning a reduced state proportional to a projection operator, the Rényi entropy of every order n > 0 equals the base-d logarithm of the rank, and they use it to express the entanglement entropy of a stabilizer state through the number of reduced stabilizer basis vectors.
quotes: What makes the Rényi entropies interesting here is that they satisfy S(n)(A) = logd(rank ρA) for all n > 0 if the state being considered has a flat entanglement spectrum i.e. it is proportional to a projection operator
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the result with its condition and give a short proof in footnote 15.

assertions.value: The authors write that S(A) = S(1)(A) equals the limit of the order-n Rényi entropy as n → 0 and that this reproduces the ordinary Von-Neumann entropy.
quotes: where S(A) = S(1)(A) = limn→0 S(n)(A) reproduces the ordinary Von-Neumann entropy.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement in the appendix that the paper does not prove.
assertions.reader_inference: The von Neumann entropy is the limit of the Rényi entropy as n approaches 1, not 0; the limit at 0 gives the log-rank (Hartley) entropy, so this looks like a typographical error. It does not affect the flat-spectrum result.

assertions.value: The authors report, for a single Pauli string with d = 3, n = 128 and w0 = 1 under a random 2-local Clifford with increasing depth over 1000 repetitions, that the estimate g = 16/9 approximately coincides with the averaged relative weight growth up to the saturation depth, and that a tighter bound is obtained with q = 2 as the base of the logarithm.

quotes: Averaged relative weight growth wD/wD−1 of a single Pauli string (d = 3, n = 128, w0 = 1) subjected to a random 2-local Clifford with increasing circuit depth D (1000 repetitions).
